Task 8: Found a genuine, previously-unaddressed inefficiency in App::apply_filter() - it cloned the entire self.packages Vec up front (self.filtered_packages = self.packages.clone()) and then used .retain() to drop non-matching rows, meaning every filtered-out package still paid the full clone cost (3 String allocations per Package) before being discarded. Restructured to filter borrowed &Package references first via .iter().filter(...), then .cloned().collect() only the survivors - same filtering order/backfill/sort behavior, pure allocation-avoidance refactor. This differs from the already-open #436/#467 (which target the per-row to_lowercase() allocation inside the filter predicate itself) - this PR targets the unconditional full-list clone that precedes and is independent of that predicate cost. Verified: cargo build --all-targets passes, cargo fmt --check clean, cargo test 394/394 pass, clippy confirmed zero new diagnostics from this change (only the pre-existing #443 cli_backend.rs errors remain, isolated and unrelated). Created draft PR #468 (branch repo-assist/perf-filter-skip-clone-non-matches-20261026). Task 5: Found a genuine, previously-unnoticed allocation bug in CliBackend::compare_versions_like's parse_parts closure: .unwrap_or((None, part.to_ascii_lowercase())) is eager (Result::unwrap_or always evaluates its arg), so to_ascii_lowercase() allocated on every version-component comparison even on the Ok/numeric path where the value is discarded. Switched to .unwrap_or_else(|_| ...) so the allocation only happens on the Err path.
